steps: Confirm the storefront pages, production domain, publishing owners and transaction flows to test in staging.
Verify page metadata, redirects and indexing, then test product discovery and the cart and checkout hand-off.
Document the release order for DNS, CDN and content publishing, including who owns the rollback.
Run the shared launch checklist with the storefront and commerce backend teams and record any fixes.
asks: Access to staging and the publishing, DNS and CDN owners
Test accounts for cart and checkout
risk: A storefront can pass page tests while checkout fails. Test the checkout hand-off with the commerce backend team before go-live.
outcome: The store team has a tested release sequence and can roll back if a critical storefront or transaction check fails.

steps: Agree the storefront events, Adobe organization, datastream and Experience Platform dataset with the data owner.
Add the analytics settings to the storefront and connect the existing consent management platform.
Test views, cart actions and purchases that the checkout emits, including a session that declines analytics consent.
Verify the agreed events in Experience Platform and hand the validation record to the data owner.
deliverables: Storefront configuration for consent and analytics
asks: Adobe organization and datastream identifiers and dataset access
A test storefront, test checkout and access to the consent platform
risk: Purchases can be missed if the checkout runs separately. Verify which events the checkout emits before accepting the measurement scope.
outcome: The data owner can see the agreed shopper events in Experience Platform and verify that analytics respects storefront consent.
